+"""Execute-time shape overrides on the unified SDPA forward engine.
+
+A graph declares the largest extent it will ever be asked for
+(``is_override_shape_enabled=True``); each ``execute`` then names the extent this
+run actually uses through ``override_uids`` / ``override_shapes`` /
+``override_strides``. The declaration is what the heuristic sees at build time,
+so the plan is chosen for the declared class rather than for the run.
+
+The measured override window and strict xfails are scoped to the SM89 Ada
+compute capability (cc 8.9) with cuDNN 9.26.0 and the selected native plan --
+the plan is pinned and asserted, so the window cannot silently move with the
+heuristics. The window was measured on an L20 and reproduces on an L40S (same cc,
+same backend, same plan); the gate deliberately does not name a board, so any
+cc 8.9 part with that backend runs it. They are observations, not portable shape
+guarantees. Other configurations still exercise the declared-shape smoke and
+malformed override-triple checks. The oversized probe has physical storage for
+every row it names, even though the graph declaration remains smaller.
+
+The contract under test belongs to the native backend, and on parts where a
+Python DSL engine also claims the graph the default selection picks that engine
+(SM120 ranks ``sdpa_fwd_prefill_sm120`` ahead of ``eng8``), so every case pins a
+backend plan explicitly and skips a part that has none. Without the pin the
+portable cases would fail on those parts for a reason that has nothing to do
+with overrides.
+
+The reference is FP64 over the same FP16 inputs. A served run measures ~3e-4
+(FP16 storage); a mis-served run is O(1) wrong, so the tolerance is not what
+decides these tests.
+"""
+
+import math
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import cudnn
+from cudnn._pygraph import pygraph
+from cudnn.engines import is_python_engine
+
+if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+    pytest.skip("needs a CUDA GPU", allow_module_level=True)
+
+pytestmark = [pytest.mark.L0, pytest.mark.skipif(cudnn.backend_version() < 92300, reason="override workspace queries need cuDNN >= 9.23")]
+
+_MEASURED_PREFILL_PLAN = "eng8_k24=1_k27=0_k38=0_k40=3_k41=1"
+_MEASURED_DECODE_PLAN = "eng8_k24=1_k27=0_k38=0_k40=2_k41=1"
+
+B, H, D = 1, 4, 64
+S_MAX = 256
+DT = cudnn.data_type.HALF
+_SCALE = 1.0 / math.sqrt(D)
+_ATOL = 5e-3
+
+
+def _reference(q, k, v, causal):
+    """FP64 reference over the *already quantized* inputs (no cuDNN, no helper)."""
+    qf, kf, vf = q.double(), k.double(), v.double()
+    scores = (qf @ kf.transpose(-1, -2)) * _SCALE
+    if causal:
+        n, m = scores.shape[-2], scores.shape[-1]
+        scores = scores.masked_fill(torch.triu(torch.ones(n, m, dtype=torch.bool, device=scores.device), 1), float("-inf"))
+    return (torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1) @ vf).float()
+
+
+class OverrideCase:
+    """One override-enabled graph with independently sized physical storage."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *, s_max=S_MAX, s_kv_max=None, causal=False, stats=False, storage_rows=None, measured=True):
+        if measured and (torch.cuda.get_device_capability() != (8, 9) or cudnn.backend_version() != 92600):
+            pytest.skip("override window measured on cc 8.9 (SM89) with cuDNN 9.26.0")
+        s_kv_max = s_max if s_kv_max is None else s_kv_max
+        self.causal = causal
+        self.stats = stats
+        self.s_max = s_max
+        self.s_kv_max = s_kv_max
+        self.q_rows = s_max if storage_rows is None else storage_rows
+        self.kv_rows = s_kv_max if storage_rows is None else storage_rows
+        g = pygraph(
+            io_data_type=DT,
+            intermediate_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+            compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+            is_override_shape_enabled=True,
+        )
+        self.graph = g
+        self.q = g.tensor(name="q", dim=[B, H, s_max, D], stride=[H * s_max * D, s_max * D, D, 1], data_type=DT)
+        self.k = g.tensor(name="k", dim=[B, H, s_kv_max, D], stride=[H * s_kv_max * D, s_kv_max * D, D, 1], data_type=DT)
+        self.v = g.tensor(name="v", dim=[B, H, s_kv_max, D], stride=[H * s_kv_max * D, s_kv_max * D, D, 1], data_type=DT)
+        if stats:
+            self.o, self.st = g.sdpa(self.q, self.k, self.v, use_causal_mask=causal, attn_scale=_SCALE, generate_stats=True)
+            self.st.set_output(True).set_data_type(cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)
+        else:
+            self.o, self.st = g.sdpa(self.q, self.k, self.v, is_inference=True, use_causal_mask=causal, attn_scale=_SCALE)
+        self.o.set_output(True).set_data_type(DT)
+        g.validate()
+        g.build_operation_graph()
+        g.create_execution_plans([cudnn.heur_mode.A, cudnn.heur_mode.FALLBACK])
+        backend = [index for index, plan in enumerate(g.plans) if not is_python_engine(plan.engine_id)]
+        if not backend:
+            pytest.skip("no native backend plan claims the override graph on this part")
+        g.select_plan(backend[0])
+        try:
+            g.check_support()
+        except cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError as error:
+            pytest.skip(f"native plan does not support this graph: {error}")
+        g.build_plans()
+        self.backend_evidence()
+        if measured:
+            name = g.get_plan_name_at_index(g._plan_index)
+            expected = _MEASURED_DECODE_PLAN if s_max == 1 else _MEASURED_PREFILL_PLAN
+            if name != expected:
+                pytest.skip(f"override window not measured for selected plan {name}")
+        self.workspace = torch.empty(max(int(g.get_workspace_size()), 1), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+        self.bufs = self.new_buffers()
+
+    def new_buffers(self):
+        """Storage covers the declaration and, for the invalid-geometry probe, the override."""
+        return (
+            torch.randn(B, H, self.q_rows, D, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda"),
+            torch.randn(B, H, self.kv_rows, D, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda"),
+            torch.randn(B, H, self.kv_rows, D, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda"),
+            torch.full((B, H, self.q_rows, D), float("nan"), dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda"),
+            torch.full((B, H, self.q_rows), float("nan"), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda"),
+        )
+
+    def execute(self, s_q, s_kv, *, bufs=None, override=True):
+        qt, kt, vt, ot, stt = self.bufs if bufs is None else bufs
+        data = {self.q: qt, self.k: kt, self.v: vt, self.o: ot}
+        kwargs = {}
+        if override:
+            q_geom, kv_geom = [B, H, s_q, D], [B, H, s_kv, D]
+            q_stride = list(qt.stride())
+            kv_stride = list(kt.stride())
+            uids = [self.q.get_uid(), self.k.get_uid(), self.v.get_uid(), self.o.get_uid()]
+            shapes = [q_geom, kv_geom, kv_geom, q_geom]
+            strides = [q_stride, kv_stride, kv_stride, q_stride]
+            if self.stats:
+                data[self.st] = stt
+                uids.append(self.st.get_uid())
+                shapes.append([B, H, s_q])
+                strides.append(list(stt.stride()))
+            kwargs = dict(override_uids=uids, override_shapes=shapes, override_strides=strides)
+        self.workspace = torch.empty(self.graph.get_workspace_size(**kwargs), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+        self.graph.execute(data, self.workspace, **kwargs)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        return ot[:, :, :s_q].float(), (stt[:, :, :s_q].double() if self.stats else None)
+
+    def assert_served(self, s_q, s_kv, *, got=None, bufs=None):
+        qt, kt, vt = (self.bufs if bufs is None else bufs)[:3]
+        o_actual, st_actual = self.execute_result if got is None else got
+        ref = _reference(qt[:, :, :s_q], kt[:, :, :s_kv], vt[:, :, :s_kv], self.causal)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(o_actual, ref, atol=_ATOL, rtol=1e-2)
+        if self.stats:
+            assert torch.isfinite(st_actual).all(), "Stats carries a non-finite value on a served override"
+            ref_lse = torch.logsumexp((qt[:, :, :s_q].double() @ kt[:, :, :s_kv].double().transpose(-1, -2)) * _SCALE, dim=-1)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(st_actual, ref_lse, atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3)
+
+    def backend_evidence(self):
+        assert self.graph.selected_engine is None
+        assert self.graph._lowered_graph is not None
+        assert self.graph._cpp_plans_created and self.graph._is_built
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "error, expected",
+    [(cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError, pytest.skip.Exception), (RuntimeError, RuntimeError)],
+    ids=["unsupported-plan-skips", "other-errors-propagate"],
+)
+def test_native_plan_support_failure(monkeypatch, error, expected):
+    def reject_support(graph):
+        raise error("native support probe")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(pygraph, "check_support", reject_support)
+    with pytest.raises(expected, match="native support probe"):
+        OverrideCase(measured=False)
+

+def case():

+
+def test_declared_shape_runs_without_any_override(case):
+    """Smoke: the declared graph is correct before an override is involved."""
+    got = case.execute(S_MAX, S_MAX, override=False)
+    case.backend_evidence()
+    ref = _reference(case.bufs[0], case.bufs[1], case.bufs[2], case.causal)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got[0], ref, atol=_ATOL, rtol=1e-2)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("s_actual", [64, 128, 192, 256], ids=lambda s: f"s{s}")
+def test_non_causal_override_on_the_tile_grid_is_served(s_actual):
+    """Non-causal overrides are served at multiples of the plan's Q tile."""

+    got = case.execute(s_actual, s_actual)

+    case.assert_served(s_actual, s_actual, got=got)

+def test_causal_override_serves_measured_lengths(s_actual):

+    case.assert_served(s_actual, s_actual, got=got)
+
+
+def test_stats_geometry_follows_the_override():

+def test_decode_graph_overrides_its_kv_extent():
+    """A decode-shaped graph (s_q = 1) serves an override of its KV extent."""
+    case = OverrideCase(s_max=1, s_kv_max=S_MAX)
+    got = case.execute(1, 64)
+    case.backend_evidence()
+    case.assert_served(1, 64, got=got)

+def test_two_extents_on_one_plan_and_a_rebind_to_fresh_buffers():
+    """Shape A, then B on the same plan, then a second buffer set.
+
+    The second run must answer for its own buffers and leave the first buffers'
+    results untouched: neither the pointer set nor the geometry of the first run
+    may be remembered.

+    case = OverrideCase()
+    first = case.execute(64, 64)
+    case.assert_served(64, 64, got=first)
+
+    # The second extent is larger, so it legitimately rewrites the first rows;
+    # what must NOT happen is the second run answering from the first run's
+    # baked-in geometry, which _assert_served checks above.
+    second = case.execute(128, 128)

+    # A third run on FRESH buffers must leave this buffer set exactly as it was.
+    fresh = case.new_buffers()

+    assert torch.isnan(case.bufs[3][:, :, 128:]).all(), "the fresh-buffer run wrote into this buffer set"
+    case.backend_evidence()

+def test_the_declared_class_decides_the_plan_not_the_run(capsys):
+    """Observation: two declarations run the same actual shape on their own plans.
+
+    No speed assertion. The point is that the plan is chosen at build time from
+    the declaration and the run does not reselect one, which is why bucketing is
+    the caller's policy rather than something the override does.
+    """
+    observations = []
+    for declared in (64, S_MAX):
+        case = OverrideCase(s_max=declared, s_kv_max=declared)

+"""The tier lists in tiers/ (README.md there) stay in step with the tree -- host-only, no kernel runs.
+
+Tripwire: every node id a list names still COLLECTS.  The modules the lists name are collected once in a child pytest (the ids are
+what ``pytest --collect-only -q`` prints from test/python), so a renamed or re-parametrized test cannot silently drop out of a tier.
+Selection pins: ``-m nightly_only`` / ``-m smoke`` select exactly the listed cells of a module -- the conftest hook applies the
+markers from the right list and runs before pytest's ``-m`` filter -- and the hook deselects nothing on its own."""
+
+import csv
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0
+
+_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+_TIERS = os.path.join(_HERE, "tiers")
+_LISTS = sorted(name for name in os.listdir(_TIERS) if name.endswith(".txt"))
+_SMOKE_ARCHES = sorted(name[len("smoke_") : -len(".txt")] for name in _LISTS if name.startswith("smoke_"))
+
+
+def _ids(name):
+    with open(os.path.join(_TIERS, name)) as fh:
+        return {line.strip() for line in fh if line.strip() and not line.lstrip().startswith("#")}
+
+
+def _collect_run(args, env=None, ok=(0,)):
+    """A child pytest collect-only run for ``args`` (from test/python, addopts cleared, no cache; a fresh test run of its own)."""
+    child_env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith("PYTEST_XDIST_") and k != "CUDNN_TEST_RUN_ID"}
+    child_env.update(env or {})
+    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "--collect-only", "-q", "-o", "addopts=", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", *args]
+    done = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=_HERE, env=child_env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=1800)
+    assert done.returncode in ok, f"child collection exited {done.returncode}:\n{done.stdout[-3000:]}\n{done.stderr[-3000:]}"
+    return done
+
+
+def _collected(done):
+    return {line.strip() for line in done.stdout.splitlines() if "::" in line and not line.startswith(" ")}
+
+
+def _collect(args, env=None, ok=(0,)):
+    """The node ids a child pytest collects for ``args``."""
+    return _collected(_collect_run(args, env, ok))
+
+
+def _module_with_most_ids(name):
+    ids = _ids(name)
+    per_module = {}
+    for nodeid in ids:
+        per_module[nodeid.split("::")[0]] = per_module.get(nodeid.split("::")[0], 0) + 1
+    module = max(per_module, key=per_module.get)

+# Test tiers: SMOKE, FULL, NIGHTLY
+
+Three nested selections of the `L0` matrix for LOCAL runs of the FROST test suites (`sdpa/frost`,
+`gated_attention_block/cutedsl`, `sdpa/graph/test_mhas_v2.py`, ...). CI keeps `-m L0` (`pytest.ini` `addopts`) and is not
+changed by anything in this directory.
+
+| tier | selection | definition | target |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| SMOKE | `-m smoke` | one cell per code path -- engine row x dtype x mask arm x layout (dense / THD / paged / split) x prepared / graph API -- at the smallest shape: `smoke_<arch>.txt` | minutes on one GPU |
+| FULL | `-m "L0 and not nightly_only"` | the functional matrix: every L0 cell minus `nightly_only.txt` | the gate for a kernel change; under an hour on 4 GPUs with 4 processes each (the `sdpa/frost` + gated-block + `test_mhas_v2` matrix measured 26.5 min with a cold and 12.5 min with a warm compiled-plan cache on Rubin, cc 10.7, 204 SMs) |
+| NIGHTLY | `-m L0`, or `-m "L0 or L1 or L2 or L3 or L4"` | everything, the `nightly_only` cells included | overnight |
+
+SMOKE is a subset of FULL, FULL of CI's L0, CI's L0 of NIGHTLY.
+
+## How the markers get on the cells
+
+`test/python/conftest.py` applies the two markers at collection from the lists here (`_apply_tier_markers`), so no test file
+carries a tier and moving a cell is a one-line edit of a list:
+
+- `smoke_<arch>.txt` -- one list per compute capability, `arch` = `cc<major><minor>` of the GPU the process runs on (`cc107`
+  on Rubin, `cc100` on B200 / GB200). A capability without a list has an EMPTY SMOKE tier -- `-m smoke` then selects nothing
+  (exit 5) and `conftest.py` says so in one `[tiers] no SMOKE list for this GPU ...` line on stderr. `CUDNN_TEST_TIER_ARCH=cc107`
+  applies another arch's list on any host (to inspect or collect it).
+- `nightly_only.txt` -- shared by every arch; `nightly_only_reasons.tsv` gives, per row, the reason and the FULL cell that
+  keeps its arm (`arm:<tokens>` = shared dtype / mask / family / shape tokens; `module` = same module only -- review those).
+- `smoke_<arch>_code_paths.tsv` -- the code path each SMOKE cell stands for (one line per listed id; the reviewer's aid).
+
+Lines are node ids relative to `test/python` (what `pytest --collect-only -q` prints from there); `#` starts a comment.
+The cc 10.7 sweep cells of `test_mhas_v2.py` (the `_cc107_sweep` functions) are defined at the default `MHAS_CC107_MULT`
+(4): the case count is part of every seed, so `[test1]` draws another geometry under a different multiplier -- a SMOKE cell
+there names the default-multiplier draw.
+`test_tiers.py` (L0) asserts that every listed id still collects and that `-m smoke` / `-m nightly_only` select exactly the
+listed cells, so a renamed or re-parametrized test cannot silently drop out of a tier -- rename the id in the list in the
+same commit.
+
+## Rules for a cell to be listed
+
+SMOKE -- every FROST engine row and every compile-time (`const_expr`) mask / layout arm the row serves is compiled and
+executed once:
+
+1. One cell per (engine row, dtype, mask arm, layout, API), at the smallest shape that reaches the arm. A shape that trips
+   a different arm (a tail tile, a ring wrap, a split) is its own code path and gets its own cell.
+2. Prefer the cell with the strongest oracle for that path (an fp32 / fp64 reference over a bitwise twin check).
+3. Host-only contract cells (declines, validators, source and SASS / PTX pins) are not SMOKE -- they cost nothing in FULL
+   and prove no kernel.
+4. A code path with no runnable L0 cell is a gap to fill in the suite, not a reason to list a non-L0 cell.
+5. A compile-time softmax LEVER is a `const_expr` arm too: `softmax_precision=HALF` (`SOFTMAX_F16`), the pre-folded scale
+   (`SCALE_PREFOLDED`) and their fused stats-less arm (`_FUSED_SHIFT_CVT`) each get one cell per kernel on the dense arm, with
+   Stats where the lever changes the LSE denominator (HALF alone, FLOAT + fold) and without where the fused arm needs it; the
+   e5m2 member of the HALF cast is covered once (the helpers are shared). The lever x mask-arm cross product, the other dtype
+   of every f16 kernel and the B / H variations stay in FULL.
+
+NIGHTLY-only -- a cell leaves FULL only with a named twin that keeps its arm (`nightly_only_reasons.tsv`, third column):
+
+1. A codegen pin -- the function BODY compiles a kernel and inspects its SASS / PTX / cubin or a PTX digest -- whose module
+   holds a numerics cell of the same dtype / mask / family / shape tokens. Classified by what the body does, never by the
+   test's name (`pin` also matches wraPPINg, sPINning and maPPINg; a test named `rendering` is as often a GPU numerics
+   test). A codegen pin with no numerics cell in its module stays in FULL.
+2. A B / H / seed twin -- a cell that differs from a kept cell of the SAME function only in batch, MHA head count or seed
+   (same engine row, mask arm, `const_expr` arm and reference; only the grid size differs). Never twinned: a function with
+   a kv-head key, or whose name mentions head / const / group / pack / gqa / mqa / thd / count / slot / budget / map /
+   prefix / metadata / parallel / capacity / degenerate / ragged / tail / sequence; an arm named in the id (gqa / mqa /
+   mha) is part of the key.
+3. A big-shape (S >= 16K) oracle cell, only when a smaller sibling of the same function keeps the arm. (None on the tree
+   today; a cell that is its own contract -- an Int32-overflow probe -- stays in FULL.)
+4. Never: `gpu_exclusive` cells, reject / decline / typed-error cells, or any cell whose demotion would change a tolerance.
+
+Counts at the time of writing: SMOKE cc 10.7 = 358 cells (266 hand-picked + 92 rule-added), cc 10.0 = 267 (135 + 132);
+NIGHTLY-only = 120 (96 codegen pins + 24 B / H / seed twins). Lists for other capabilities are added as they are reviewed.
+
+## Running
+
+From `test/python`, with the FROST engines opted in (`CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1`); keep the `sdpa/frost/` paths
+contiguous on the command line (`test/AGENTS.md`):
+
+```bash
+pytest -m smoke -n 4 --dist loadgroup sdpa/frost gated_attention_block/cutedsl sdpa/graph/test_mhas_v2.py   # SMOKE, one GPU
+pytest -m "L0 and not nightly_only" sdpa/frost gated_attention_block/cutedsl sdpa/graph/test_mhas_v2.py      # FULL
+```
+
+Several pytest processes on one GPU: set `CUDNN_TEST_SHARED_GPU=1` in each so the GPU memory gate of `conftest.py` is armed
+for them (see `test/AGENTS.md`).

+repacks elsewhere, the output following q), the masked-row contract (o = 0, lse = -inf), CUDA-graph capture, the execute-path contract

+the GPU-free contract tests (the lazy export in every import order, the signature pin, mask_to_kv_lengths, the reference, the declines
+a declaration raises before any device work); the prefix-mask form (``mask_is_prefix=True``: the lengths derived on the device by ONE
+launch of the row-popcount kernel, no cast pass, no host synchronisation) bitwise against both lengths routes, its debug check, its
+allocation-free execute, its CUDA-graph capture, the kernel's own pins (bitwise the torch row count on every shape and layout on ANY
+CUDA device, allocation- and sync-free with ``out`` given, graph-captured, the typed DSL-floor decline).  The acceptance grid is one cell
+per (key-mask form, tile width, bias-staging class): the kernel paths are pinned per body by the sdpa modules, and B = 2 is bitwise two
+B = 1 calls (its own pin below).

+Tolerances are the SM107 f16 row's own (test_sdpa_bias_sm107.py), not widened for this layer: O against the fp64 oracle at
+atol 5e-2 / rtol 3e-2 (an fp32 accumulation, one 16-bit rounding at the store), the LSE at 1e-4 / 1e-4 (the bias enters the fp32 score
+by one FFMA of bias * (1 / scale), then the scale multiply).  The reference reads the bf16 bias the kernel reads.

+    submodule on its parent, bypassing the lazy table) -- the package module is callable, so every spelling runs the function."""
+    code = f"""
+import cudnn
+order = {order!r}
+if order == "symbol_first":
+    f = cudnn.triangle_attention
+elif order == "package_first":
+    import cudnn.triangle_attention
+    f = cudnn.triangle_attention
+else:

+    f = cudnn.triangle_attention

+print(type(f).__name__)

+    parameter (no ``*`` before it -- a caller passing it positionally runs there and must run here); the four additions are keyword-only

+    assert p["mask_is_prefix"].default is False and p["check_prefix_mask"].default is None
+    assert tapi.CUEQ_SIGNATURE_VERSION == "0.12.0"

+def test_prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths_is_the_sync_free_twin(monkeypatch):
+    """GPU-free (CPU tensors): the device-side helper returns each row's True count as int32 (B, N, 1, 1, 1) -- equal to mask_to_kv_lengths
+    on a prefix mask -- writes into a caller's ``out`` (the ``workspace`` keyword of the two-kernel form is accepted and unused: the fused
+    kernel stages nothing, ``prefix_mask_workspace_bytes`` is 0), raises the typed contract error on a non-prefix mask ONLY with the check
+    on (kwarg or the environment), and serves the count otherwise (documented)."""
+    b, n, s = 2, 5, 11
+    lengths = torch.tensor([[7, 0, 11, 1, 5], [3, 11, 0, 4, 9]], dtype=torch.int32).view(b, n, 1, 1, 1)
+    prefix = torch.arange(s).view(1, 1, 1, 1, s) < lengths
+    got = tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(prefix)
+    assert got.dtype == torch.int32 and tuple(got.shape) == (b, n, 1, 1, 1) and torch.equal(got, lengths) and torch.equal(got, tapi.mask_to_kv_lengths(prefix))
+    out = torch.empty(b, n, 1, 1, 1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    assert tapi.prefix_mask_workspace_bytes(b, n, s) == 0, "the fused derivation stages nothing"
+    ws = torch.empty(4 * b * n * s, dtype=torch.uint8)  # a buffer sized by the two-kernel form's recipe: accepted, untouched
+    ws.fill_(0xA5)
+    assert tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(prefix, out, workspace=ws, check=True) is out and torch.equal(out, lengths)
+    assert (ws == 0xA5).all(), "the workspace is not written by the fused derivation"
+    holed = prefix.clone()
+    holed[0, 0, 0, 0, 2] = False  # a hole inside the live prefix: not a prefix mask
+    assert tapi.mask_to_kv_lengths(holed) is None
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"PREFIX-shaped .* 1 of the 10 \(b, n\) rows .* \[\[0, 0\]\]"):
+        tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(holed, check=True)
+    monkeypatch.setenv(tapi.CHECK_PREFIX_MASK_ENV, "1")
+    assert tapi.prefix_check_enabled()
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="PREFIX-shaped"):

+    monkeypatch.delenv(tapi.CHECK_PREFIX_MASK_ENV)
+    counted = tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(holed)  # the default: no check, the row's True count (7 - 1 = 6) -- the documented behaviour
+    assert counted[0, 0].item() == 6 and torch.equal(counted.view(-1)[1:], lengths.view(-1)[1:])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="boolean"):

+    assert torch.equal(tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(prefix, workspace=torch.empty(8, dtype=torch.uint8)), lengths)  # any size: unused
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="workspace must be a contiguous uint8"):

+def test_reference_is_the_formula_and_keeps_the_empty_row_contract():

+def _desc(shape, stride, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"):

+    return _desc((b, n, h, s, d), (n * s * h * d, s * h * d, d, h * d, 1), dtype, device)

+    return _desc((b, n, h, s, d), (n * h * s * d, h * s * d, s * d, d, 1), dtype, device)
+

+    return _desc((bb, 1, h, s_q, s_kv), (h * s_q * row, h * s_q * row, s_q * row, row, 1), dtype, device)

+@requires_cuda
+def test_execute_declines_an_output_whose_byte_range_intersects_an_operand_before_any_launch():
+    """`o` and the lse (the kernel writes them) must be disjoint from every tensor it reads, as BYTE RANGES, not by pointer equality: an `o`
+    view starting inside q (two views over one allocation) has a distinct data_ptr and the kernel would overwrite rows it has still to read.
+    Host-side on any CUDA device (the check precedes compile and launch); inputs may overlap each other (q / k / v as slices of one buffer are
+    read-only); a disjoint `o` of the same allocation passes."""
+    b, n, h, s, d = 1, 16, 4, 64, 32
+    plan = tapi.TriangleAttentionFwd(_left_desc(b, n, h, s, d), _left_desc(b, n, h, s, d), _left_desc(b, n, h, s, d), _bias_desc(1, h, s, s), lse=True)
+    numel = n * s * h * d
+    buf = torch.empty(3 * numel, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    view = lambda start: buf[start : start + numel].view(b, n, s, h, d).permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4)  # noqa: E731
+    q, k, v = view(0), view(0), view(0)  # q, k, v over ONE buffer: read-only, admitted
+    bias = torch.empty(1, 1, h, s, s, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    lse = torch.empty(b, n, h, s, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    plan._check_execute_args(q, k, v, bias, None, view(numel), lse, None, None, None)  # a disjoint o of the same allocation
+    o_half = view(numel // 2)
+    assert o_half.data_ptr() != q.data_ptr()  # the old pointer-equality test saw distinct pointers
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"o must not alias q: their byte ranges intersect"):
+        plan._check_execute_args(q, k, v, bias, None, o_half, lse, None, None, None)
+    # o over the bias, and o over the lse (two outputs)
+    bbuf = torch.empty(numel + h * s * s // 2, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    bias_v = bbuf[: h * s * s].view(1, 1, h, s, s)
+    o_b = bbuf[h * s * s // 2 : h * s * s // 2 + numel].view(b, n, s, h, d).permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="o must not alias bias"):
+        plan._check_execute_args(q, k, v, bias_v, None, o_b, lse, None, None, None)
+    lbuf = torch.empty(2 * numel, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    lse_v = lbuf[: 2 * n * h * s].view(torch.float32).view(b, n, h, s)
+    o_l = lbuf[n * h * s : n * h * s + numel].view(b, n, s, h, d).permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="o must not alias lse"):
+        plan._check_execute_args(q, k, v, bias, None, o_l, lse_v, None, None, None)

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Rubin: the acceptance grid, the layouts, the masked rows, CUDA graphs, autograd, the live declines
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+def _act(b, n, h, s, d, *, dtype, gen, layout="left"):
+    if layout == "left":  # (B, N, S, H, D) storage presented as (B, N, H, S, D): the zero-copy form
+        return torch.randn(b, n, s, h, d, generator=gen, device="cuda", dtype=dtype).permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4)
+    return torch.randn(b, n, h, s, d, generator=gen, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)  # cuEquivariance-contiguous (head-major)
+
+
+def _inputs(s, d, *, b=1, n=None, h=4, h_kv=None, dtype=torch.bfloat16, seed=0, layout="left", bias_form="h", bias_dtype=None, s_q=None):
+    n = n or s
+    s_q = s_q or s
+    h_kv = h_kv or h
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    q = _act(b, n, h, s_q, d, dtype=dtype, gen=gen, layout=layout)
+    k = _act(b, n, h_kv, s, d, dtype=dtype, gen=gen, layout=layout)
+    v = _act(b, n, h_kv, s, d, dtype=dtype, gen=gen, layout=layout)
+    bb = b if bias_form.startswith("b") else 1
+    hh = h if "h" in bias_form else 1
+    bias = torch.randn(bb, 1, hh, s_q, s, generator=gen, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) * 2.0
+    bias = bias.to(bias_dtype or dtype)
+    return q, k, v, bias, gen
+
+
+def _lengths(b, n, s, gen, *, empty_rows=()):
+    lengths = torch.randint(1, s + 1, (b, n, 1, 1, 1), generator=gen, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    for bi, ni in empty_rows:
+        lengths[bi, ni] = 0
+    return lengths
+
+
+def _dense_mask(b, n, s, gen, *, empty_rows=()):
+    mask = torch.rand(b, n, 1, 1, s, generator=gen, device="cuda") < 0.7
+    mask[..., 0] = True  # at least one live key per row
+    for bi, ni in empty_rows:
+        mask[bi, ni] = False
+    return mask
+
+
+def _reference(q, k, v, bias, *, mask=None, kv_lengths=None, scale=None):
+    """Per outer entry to bound the fp64 scores' memory."""
+    outs = []
+    for bi in range(q.shape[0]):
+        bb = bias[bi : bi + 1] if bias.shape[0] > 1 else bias
+        outs.append(
+            tref.triangle_attention_reference(
+                q[bi : bi + 1],
+                k[bi : bi + 1],
+                v[bi : bi + 1],
+                bb,
+                mask=None if mask is None else mask[bi : bi + 1],
+                scale=scale,
+                kv_lengths=None if kv_lengths is None else kv_lengths[bi : bi + 1],
+            )
+        )
+    return tuple(torch.cat([o[i] for o in outs], dim=0) for i in range(3))
+
+
+def _check(o, ref, lse=None):
+    """Keyless rows EXACTLY 0 / -inf (never NaN, never a residue); live rows against the fp64 oracle at the row's tolerances."""
+    o_ref, lse_ref, _ = ref
+    empty = torch.isneginf(lse_ref)
+    assert torch.isfinite(o).all(), "o has a non-finite value"
+    assert (o[empty] == 0).all(), "a keyless row's o must be exactly 0"
+    torch.testing.assert_close(o[~empty].double(), o_ref[~empty], **_TOL_O)
+    if lse is not None:
+        assert torch.isneginf(lse[empty]).all(), "a keyless row's lse must be exactly -inf"
+        torch.testing.assert_close(lse[~empty].double(), lse_ref[~empty], **_TOL_LSE)
+
+
+def _no_copies():
+    c = tapi.copy_counters()
+    return c.get("fallback_copies", 0) == 0, c
+
+
+# One cell per (key-mask form, tile width, bias-staging class) at B 1 (B 2 is bitwise two B 1 calls: the dedicated pins below).  (S, D, form):
+# the 64-wide pair resident block at the padded-stride bias tail (217, all three forms), the pair n4 resident block at 128 (384), the
+# one-batch-entry streamed ring and the S_q % 256 guard (512 none), the pair n8 resident at 64 under lengths / under the word (512), the
+# TMEM-Q bias-only body (256 at D 64), the d64 pair ring at 128 with 3 stages (512 at D 64 none), the 64-wide d64 ring under lengths / the
+# word -- the latter the TMEM-Q bias + mask body (512 at D 64), one 64-column kv tile with both resident arms (64 mask), and the d64
+# padded-stride bias tail under the word (217 at D 64 mask: no sdpa module runs a d64 bias tail).
+_GRID = [
+    (217, 32, "none"),
+    (217, 32, "kv_lengths"),
+    (217, 32, "mask"),
+    (384, 32, "none"),
+    (512, 32, "none"),
+    (512, 32, "kv_lengths"),
+    (512, 32, "mask"),
+    (256, 64, "none"),
+    (512, 64, "none"),
+    (512, 64, "kv_lengths"),
+    (512, 64, "mask"),
+    (64, 32, "mask"),
+    (217, 64, "mask"),
+]
+

+@requires_rubin
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("s, d, form", _GRID, ids=[f"{s}-{d}-{form}" for s, d, form in _GRID])
+def test_function_matches_the_fp64_reference(s, d, form):
+    """The drop-in on the zero-copy layout over the acceptance grid: S (one tile, the budget edges, a tail at 217 whose bias is padded,
+    the streamed ring above the resident budget), D 32 / 64, the three key-mask forms with empty rows on both mask forms.  No layout copy
+    except the documented bias pad at S % 8 != 0."""
+    b = 1
+    q, k, v, bias, gen = _inputs(s, d, seed=s * 7 + d)
+    kw = {}
+    if form == "kv_lengths":
+        kw["kv_lengths"] = _lengths(b, s, s, gen, empty_rows=((0, 1),))
+    elif form == "mask":
+        kw["mask"] = _dense_mask(b, s, s, gen, empty_rows=((0, 3),))
+    tapi.reset_copy_counters()
+    o = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, **kw)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert tuple(o.shape) == tuple(q.shape) and o.dtype == q.dtype and tuple(o.stride()) == tuple(q.stride()), (o.stride(), q.stride())
+    clean, counts = _no_copies()
+    if s % 8:
+        assert counts == {"bias_repack": 1, "fallback_copies": 1}, counts  # the documented pad of a compact bias at S_kv % 8 != 0
+    else:
+        assert clean, counts
+    _check(o, _reference(q, k, v, bias, **kw))
+    o2 = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, **kw)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(o, o2), "two launches differ"

+def test_workspace_is_sized_and_carved_by_the_sdpa_adapters_recipe():
+    """GPU-free: the kv_lengths form's Q-side lengths are the second chunk of the SDPA adapters' shared carve (`ws_align` 128-byte chunks,
+    `WorkspaceCarver`), so they start at `ws_align(plan bytes)`; the other forms need exactly the plan's bytes; a missing or short buffer
+    raises the shared carver's own error (never a local variant)."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.api_dsl import ws_align
+
+    wb = tapi.workspace_bytes
+    assert wb(0, 0) == 0 and wb(1024, 0) == 1024
+    assert wb(0, 217) == ws_align(4 * 217) == 896 and wb(100, 217) == 128 + 896 and wb(256, 5) == 256 + 128 and wb(257, 1) == 384 + 128
+    buf = torch.empty(wb(100, 217), dtype=torch.uint8)  # a CPU buffer: the carve is a pure view arithmetic
+    plan_ws, q_lens = tapi.carve_workspace(buf, 100, 217, "TriangleAttentionFwd")
+    assert plan_ws.dtype == torch.uint8 and plan_ws.numel() == 100 and plan_ws.data_ptr() == buf.data_ptr()
+    assert q_lens.dtype == torch.int32 and tuple(q_lens.shape) == (217,) and q_lens.data_ptr() - buf.data_ptr() == 128
+    assert tapi.carve_workspace(buf[:896], 0, 217, "TriangleAttentionFwd")[1].data_ptr() == buf.data_ptr()  # no plan bytes: the lengths lead
+    # the prefix_mask form's two more chunks, in order: the derived KV lengths (B * N words), then the mask staging (B * N * S_kv words)
+    assert wb(100, 217, 434, 2 * 217 * 217) == ws_align(100) + ws_align(4 * 217) + ws_align(4 * 434) + ws_align(4 * 2 * 217 * 217) == 379648
+    assert wb(0, 0, 0, 0) == 0 and wb(100, 0, 0, 0) == 100 and wb(0, 0, 5, 0) == 128
+    buf3 = torch.empty(wb(100, 217, 434, 2 * 217 * 217), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    p, q, kv, st = tapi.carve_workspace_chunks(buf3, 100, 217, 434, 2 * 217 * 217, "TriangleAttentionFwd")
+    assert [t.data_ptr() - buf3.data_ptr() for t in (p, q, kv, st)] == [0, 128, 1024, 2816]
+    assert kv.dtype == st.dtype == torch.int32 and kv.numel() == 434 and st.numel() == 2 * 217 * 217
+    assert tapi.carve_workspace_chunks(buf3, 100, 217, 0, 0, "TriangleAttentionFwd")[2:] == (None, None)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"TriangleAttentionFwd requires a 1024-byte workspace but execute\(\) received none"):
+        tapi.carve_workspace(None, 100, 217, "TriangleAttentionFwd")
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="requires a 1024-byte workspace; the provided buffer has only 1000 bytes"):
+        tapi.carve_workspace(buf[:1000], 100, 217, "TriangleAttentionFwd")

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("form", ["mask", "kv_lengths", "prefix_mask"])
+def test_execute_allocates_nothing_and_never_synchronizes(form):
+    """Every key-mask form: a warm execute allocates no device memory (the allocator's allocation COUNT is unchanged too, so no temporary
+    hides behind a freed buffer) and issues no host synchronisation -- on the kv_lengths form the Q-side lengths the graph's padding
+    contract requires are written into the CALLER's workspace (an async memset), never allocated; on the prefix_mask form the derived KV
+    lengths land in the caller's workspace as well, written by the one-launch derivation kernel straight from the boolean mask (no cast
+    pass, no staging: the workspace carries no mask chunk)."""
+    s = 128
+    q, k, v, bias, gen = _inputs(s, 32, seed=17)
+    mask = _dense_mask(1, s, s, gen) if form == "mask" else None
+    lengths = _lengths(1, s, s, gen, empty_rows=((0, 4),)) if form != "mask" else None
+    if form == "prefix_mask":
+        mask, lengths = (torch.arange(s, device="cuda").view(1, 1, 1, 1, s) < lengths), None
+    plan = tapi.TriangleAttentionFwd(q, k, v, bias, mask=(form != "kv_lengths"), kv_lengths=(form == "kv_lengths"), mask_is_prefix=(form == "prefix_mask"))
+    plan.check_support()
+    plan.compile()
+    if form == "kv_lengths":
+        assert plan.get_workspace_size() == tapi.workspace_bytes(plan._plan_workspace_bytes, s) >= 4 * s
+    elif form == "prefix_mask":
+        assert plan.get_workspace_size() == tapi.workspace_bytes(plan._plan_workspace_bytes, s, s) >= 4 * s + 4 * s
+        assert plan.get_workspace_size() < tapi.workspace_bytes(
+            plan._plan_workspace_bytes, s, s, s * s
+        ), "no mask staging chunk: the fused kernel reads the mask"
+    o = tapi._bshd_empty(*q.shape, q.dtype, q.device)
+    ws = torch.empty(max(plan.get_workspace_size(), 1), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, lengths, o, None, None, ws if plan.get_workspace_size() else None, mask=mask)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    before = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
+    before_count = torch.cuda.memory_stats()["allocation.all.allocated"]
+    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+    try:
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, lengths, o, None, None, ws if plan.get_workspace_size() else None, mask=mask)
+    finally:
+        torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("default")
+    assert torch.cuda.memory_allocated() == before
+    assert torch.cuda.memory_stats()["allocation.all.allocated"] == before_count, "a device allocation (even a freed temporary) inside execute"
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    ref_lengths = tapi.mask_to_kv_lengths(mask) if form == "prefix_mask" else lengths
+    _check(o, _reference(q, k, v, bias, mask=mask if form == "mask" else None, kv_lengths=ref_lengths))
+    if form == "kv_lengths":
+        _plan_ws, q_lens = tapi.carve_workspace(ws, plan._plan_workspace_bytes, s, "TriangleAttentionFwd")  # the same carve execute ran
+        assert (q_lens == s).all(), "the Q-side lengths chunk must hold S_q on every entry"
+        assert (o[0, 4] == 0).all()
+    elif form == "prefix_mask":
+        _plan_ws, q_lens, kv_lens, stage = tapi.carve_workspace_chunks(ws, plan._plan_workspace_bytes, s, s, 0, "TriangleAttentionFwd")
+        assert (q_lens == s).all() and torch.equal(kv_lens.view(1, s, 1, 1, 1), ref_lengths), "the derived KV lengths live in the caller's workspace"
+        assert stage is None and (o[0, 4] == 0).all()

+def test_cuda_graph_capture_replays_bitwise_and_follows_new_data():

+        tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=mask, out=out)

+    torch.cuda.synchronize()

+    q.copy_(q_new)

+    g.replay()

+    assert torch.equal(out, eager_new)

+    plan.check_support()
+    plan.compile()
+    out2 = tapi._bshd_empty(*q.shape, q.dtype, q.device)
+    ws = torch.empty(max(plan.get_workspace_size(), 1), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    g2 = plan.make_cuda_graph(q, k, v, bias, None, out2, None, ws if plan.get_workspace_size() else None, mask=mask)
+    out2.fill_(float("nan"))
+    g2.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out2, eager_new)
+    # the kv_lengths form: the workspace fill (the Q-side lengths) is captured with the launches and the replay follows new lengths
+    lengths = _lengths(1, s, s, gen, empty_rows=((0, 3),))
+    eager_len = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths=lengths)

+    g3 = plan_l.make_cuda_graph(q, k, v, bias, lengths, out3, None, ws_l)

+        tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=holed, mask_is_prefix=True, check_prefix_mask=True)
+    monkeypatch.setenv(tapi.CHECK_PREFIX_MASK_ENV, "1")
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="PREFIX-shaped"):
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=holed, mask_is_prefix=True)  # the environment turns the check on
+    o_forced = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=holed, mask_is_prefix=True, check_prefix_mask=False)  # an explicit False wins
+    monkeypatch.delenv(tapi.CHECK_PREFIX_MASK_ENV)
+    o_default = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=holed, mask_is_prefix=True)
+    counts = tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(holed)
+    assert counts[0, 0].item() == 200 - 37 and counts[0, 7].item() == lengths[0, 7].item() + 1 and counts[0, 5].item() == 0
+    o_counts = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths=counts)
+    o_dense = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=holed)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(o_default, o_counts) and torch.equal(o_forced, o_counts), "a non-prefix row is served as the prefix of its True count"
+    assert not torch.equal(o_default, o_dense), "the dense mask attends the holed keys; the prefix form cannot"
+    assert torch.equal(o_default[0, 1:5], o_dense[0, 1:5]) and (o_default[0, 5] == 0).all()  # the prefix rows agree, the empty row reads 0
+    _check(o_default, _reference(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths=counts))
+    plan = tapi.TriangleAttentionFwd(q, k, v, bias, mask=True, mask_is_prefix=True)
+    plan.check_support()
+    plan.compile()
+    o = tapi._bshd_empty(*q.shape, q.dtype, q.device)
+    ws = torch.empty(plan.get_workspace_size(), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="PREFIX-shaped"):
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, None, o, None, None, ws, mask=holed, check_prefix_mask=True)
+    plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, None, o, None, None, ws, mask=holed)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(o, o_counts)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="requires a boolean mask"):
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask_is_prefix=True)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="mask_is_prefix=True; kv_lengths must be None"):
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, counts, o, None, None, ws, mask=holed)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="mask_is_prefix=True; a boolean"):
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, None, o, None, None, ws)
+
+
+@requires_rubin
+def test_prefix_mask_form_captures_into_a_cuda_graph_and_follows_the_mask_contents():
+    """The prefix form's derivation runs on the device only, so a CUDA graph captures the whole call (the Q-side memset, the mask cast,
+    the row count, the launches) and a replay re-derives the lengths from the mask's CURRENT contents: bitwise the eager kv_lengths call
+    before and after the mask changes, on the class API (make_cuda_graph) and on the drop-in function (torch.cuda.graph)."""
+    s = 256
+    q, k, v, bias, gen = _inputs(s, 32, seed=27)
+    lengths = _lengths(1, s, s, gen, empty_rows=((0, 3),))
+    mask = torch.arange(s, device="cuda").view(1, 1, 1, 1, s) < lengths
+    eager = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths=lengths)
+    plan = tapi.TriangleAttentionFwd(q, k, v, bias, mask=True, mask_is_prefix=True)
+    plan.check_support()
+    plan.compile()
+    out = tapi._bshd_empty(*q.shape, q.dtype, q.device)
+    ws = torch.empty(plan.get_workspace_size(), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    g = plan.make_cuda_graph(q, k, v, bias, None, out, None, ws, mask=mask)
+    out.fill_(float("nan"))
+    ws.fill_(0)  # a replay must re-derive the lengths (and re-write the Q-side ones), not rely on a previous call's chunks
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    g.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out, eager) and (out[0, 3] == 0).all()
+    new_lengths = _lengths(1, s, s, gen, empty_rows=((0, 9),))
+    mask.copy_(torch.arange(s, device="cuda").view(1, 1, 1, 1, s) < new_lengths)
+    eager_new = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths=new_lengths)
+    g.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out, eager_new) and (out[0, 9] == 0).all() and not torch.equal(eager, eager_new)
+    # the drop-in function under torch.cuda.graph (warm first; the per-call workspace is the graph pool's)
+    out_f = tapi._bshd_empty(*q.shape, q.dtype, q.device)
+    side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=mask, mask_is_prefix=True, out=out_f)
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(side)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    gf = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(gf, stream=side):
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=mask, mask_is_prefix=True, out=out_f)
+    out_f.fill_(float("nan"))
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    gf.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out_f, eager_new)
+    mask.copy_(torch.arange(s, device="cuda").view(1, 1, 1, 1, s) < lengths)
+    gf.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out_f, eager)
+
+
+@requires_cuda
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("b,n,s", [(1, 2, 0), (1, 3, 7), (1, 256, 217), (1, 8, 5000), (3, 33, 1023)])
+def test_prefix_lengths_kernel_is_bitwise_the_torch_row_count_on_every_shape(b, n, s):
+    """The one-launch derivation on ANY CUDA device (the kernel is arch-generic): the counts of a random, NON-prefix mask with all-False and
+    all-True rows equal ``mask.sum(-1, dtype=int32)`` bitwise -- S_kv = 0, below one warp, not a multiple of 8 / 32 / 128 (217, 1023), many
+    words (5000), B > 1 -- on the contiguous mask and on strided views of a wider buffer (a batch slice, a padded row stride, two strided key
+    views) in every cell."""
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(b * 1000003 + n * 1009 + s)
+    mask = torch.rand(b, n, 1, 1, s, generator=gen, device="cuda") < 0.6 if s else torch.zeros(b, n, 1, 1, 0, dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda")
+    if n > 2:
+        mask[0, 1] = False
+        mask[-1, 2] = True
+    ref = mask.sum(-1, dtype=torch.int32).view(b, n, 1, 1, 1)
+    out = torch.full((b, n, 1, 1, 1), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    assert tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(mask, out, check=False) is out
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out, ref)
+    assert torch.equal(tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(mask, check=False), ref)  # the allocating form
+    if s == 0:
+        return
+    wide = torch.rand(b + 1, n + 6, 1, 1, 3 * s + 16, generator=gen, device="cuda") < 0.5
+    views = (wide[1:, :n, :, :, :s], wide[:b, 3 : 3 + n, :, :, 7 : 7 + s], wide[:b, :n, :, :, ::2][..., :s], wide[:b, 2 : 2 + n, :, :, 1::3][..., :s])
+    for view in views:
+        assert tuple(view.shape) == (b, n, 1, 1, s)
+        got = tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(view, check=False)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(got, view.sum(-1, dtype=torch.int32).view(b, n, 1, 1, 1)), tuple(view.stride())
+
+
+@requires_cuda
+def test_prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths_allocates_nothing_never_synchronizes_and_captures():
+    """With ``out`` given the derivation is ONE launch into the caller's memory: a warm call allocates nothing (the allocator's allocation
+    COUNT is unchanged, so no temporary hides behind a freed buffer) and issues no host synchronisation; a CUDA graph captures it and a
+    replay re-derives the counts from the mask's CURRENT contents, bitwise the torch row count."""
+    b, n, s = 2, 300, 333
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(7)
+    mask = torch.rand(b, n, 1, 1, s, generator=gen, device="cuda") < 0.5
+    out = torch.empty(b, n, 1, 1, 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(mask, out, check=False)  # warm: the artifact is built / loaded
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    before, before_count = torch.cuda.memory_allocated(), torch.cuda.memory_stats()["allocation.all.allocated"]
+    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+    try:
+        tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(mask, out, check=False)
+    finally:
+        torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("default")
+    assert torch.cuda.memory_allocated() == before
+    assert torch.cuda.memory_stats()["allocation.all.allocated"] == before_count, "a device allocation (even a freed temporary) inside the derivation"
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out, mask.sum(-1, dtype=torch.int32).view(b, n, 1, 1, 1))
+    side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+        tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(mask, out, check=False)
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(side)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(g, stream=side):
+        tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(mask, out, check=False)
+    out.fill_(-1)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    g.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out, mask.sum(-1, dtype=torch.int32).view(b, n, 1, 1, 1))
+    mask.copy_(torch.rand(b, n, 1, 1, s, generator=gen, device="cuda") < 0.2)
+    g.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out, mask.sum(-1, dtype=torch.int32).view(b, n, 1, 1, 1))
+
+
+@requires_cuda
+def test_prefix_lengths_kernel_declines_a_too_old_dsl_typed(monkeypatch):
+    """Rule 7: a DSL below the FROST floor is a typed NotImplementedError naming the installed version and the floor, raised by the kernel
+    module's own gate before any compile (the per-device plan cache is cleared around the probe so the gate runs; the cleared cache is
+    rebuilt by the call that follows)."""
+    from cudnn.frost import buffers
+    from cudnn.triangle_attention.kernels import prefix_lengths as pl
+
+    mask = torch.ones(1, 2, 1, 1, 9, dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda")
+    pl.prefix_lengths_plan.cache_clear()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(buffers, "cutedsl_state", lambda: (True, ("nvidia-cutlass-dsl", "4.6.2")))
+    try:
+        assert "4.6.2" in pl.requirement_error(mask.device.index or 0)
+        with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match=r"requires nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4\.7\.0; found 4\.6\.2"):
+            tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(mask, check=False)
+    finally:
+        monkeypatch.undo()
+        pl.prefix_lengths_plan.cache_clear()
+    assert pl.requirement_error(mask.device.index or 0) is None
+    assert torch.equal(tapi.prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(mask, check=False).view(-1), torch.tensor([9, 9], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"))
+
+
+@requires_rubin
+def test_return_aux_is_a_typed_decline_quoting_the_engine():
+    """The row max is a side output the engine row's bias arm does not store: return_aux=True is declined with the ENGINE's reason; so is
+    a head dim the bias arm is not wired on (D 128 with a bias: the row names its d32 / d64 flavors) through the drop-in function."""
+    q, k, v, bias, gen = _inputs(128, 32, seed=20)
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="score side outputs") as info:
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, return_aux=True)
+    assert tapi.ENGINE_ROW in str(info.value)
+    q128, k128, v128, bias128, _ = _inputs(128, 128, seed=20)
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="d32, d64") as info:
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q128, k128, v128, bias128)
+    assert tapi.ENGINE_ROW in str(info.value)
+
+
+@requires_rubin
+def test_autograd_forward_is_served_and_the_backward_is_a_typed_decline():
+    s = 128
+    q, k, v, bias, gen = _inputs(s, 32, seed=21)
+    q.requires_grad_(True)
+    bias.requires_grad_(True)
+    o = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias)
+    assert o.grad_fn is not None and o.requires_grad
+    _check(o.detach(), _reference(q.detach(), k, v, bias.detach()))
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="no backward registered yet"):
+        o.float().sum().backward()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        o2 = tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias)
+    assert o2.grad_fn is None and torch.equal(o2, o.detach())
+
+
+@requires_rubin
+def test_rejects_on_a_live_device_are_typed():
+    s = 128
+    q, k, v, bias, gen = _inputs(s, 32, seed=22)
+    lengths = _lengths(1, s, s, gen)
+    mask = torch.arange(s, device="cuda").view(1, 1, 1, 1, s) < lengths
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not both"):
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=mask, kv_lengths=lengths)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="rank 5"):
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q[0], k[0], v[0], bias[0])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="boolean"):
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=mask.to(torch.float32))
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="int32"):
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths=lengths.to(torch.int64))
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="bf16 and fp16"):
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), k.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), v.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), bias)
+    q20, k20, v20, bias20, _ = _inputs(s, 24, seed=23)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="multiple of 8"):  # the FE graph contract itself refuses D % 8 != 0 (a malformed sdpa node)
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q20[..., :20], k20[..., :20], v20[..., :20], bias20)
+    q128, k128, v128, bias128, _ = _inputs(s, 128, seed=24)
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="flavors") as info:
+        tapi.triangle_attention(q128, k128, v128, bias128)
+    assert tapi.ENGINE_ROW in str(info.value)
+    plan = tapi.TriangleAttentionFwd(q, k, v, bias, kv_lengths=True)
+    plan.check_support()
+    plan.compile()
+    o = tapi._bshd_empty(*q.shape, q.dtype, q.device)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="kv_lengths=True"):
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, None, o)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="never allocates"):
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, lengths, None)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"requires a \d+-byte workspace but execute\(\) received none"):  # the shared carver's error
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, lengths, o)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="16-byte aligned"):  # the shared carver's base rule (the lengths' reader needs 4; a torch allocation is 512)
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, lengths, o, None, None, torch.empty(plan.get_workspace_size() + 8, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")[8:])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="contiguous"):  # the one check the carver leaves to the API: a strided buffer would be carved on a copy
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, lengths, o, None, None, torch.empty(2 * plan.get_workspace_size(), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")[::2])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="strides"):
+        plan.execute(q.contiguous(), k, v, bias, lengths, o)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="lse=False"):
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, lengths, o, torch.empty(1, s, 4, s, device="cuda"))
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="score_max"):
+        plan.execute(q, k, v, bias, lengths, o, None, torch.empty(1, s, 4, s, device="cuda"))
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="score side outputs"):
+        tapi.TriangleAttentionFwd(q, k, v, bias, score_max=True).check_support()
